findings.evidence: "Predictable mistake: yes" paired with "Suggested fix: none"
findings.fix: Add a preventive fix, such as restricting the code field to exactly 6 digit characters (e.g. six separate boxes, or a mask that blocks a 7th keystroke) so the mistake can't occur.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - first message block (wrong digit count)
findings.violation: The entry identifies this as a predictable, foreseeable mistake but proposes no design change to prevent it, leaving the error to recur indefinitely.

findings.evidence: "Request a new code and enter it here."
findings.fix: Add a resend-code action to the error state itself (as this entry's own suggested fix proposes), or point the message to an existing resend control elsewhere on the screen.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - second message block (expired code)
findings.violation: The message instructs the user to request a new code, but the error is delivered as static inline text with no control to actually do that, so the requested action is unavailable where the error appears.

findings.fix: Clear the field for this error, unlike the digit-count error where preserving input is appropriate, so the user isn't invited to resubmit the same expired value.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - second message block (expired code)
findings.violation: Preserving the expired code is misleading, since that exact value can never become valid again; the user may simply resubmit it instead of realizing a wholly new code is required.

findings.evidence: "selectable, offers a resend code button in place of the message"
findings.fix: Update the "Container" field to match the proposed fix (e.g. "interactive"/"button"), or reword "Suggested fix" to make clear it describes a future state, not the current one.
findings.location: Two-factor setup, verification code - second message block (expired code), Suggested fix field
findings.violation: "Selectable" contradicts this same entry's own "Container: inline" value, leaving the record internally inconsistent about whether the error is static text or an interactive control.

findings.fix: Include the year, e.g. "This promo code ended on 30 June 2026."

findings.violation: The date omits the year, so the user can't tell how long ago the code expired, and the message is ambiguous near a year boundary.

findings.evidence: "Predictable mistake: yes" paired with "Suggested fix: none"
findings.fix: Prevent the mismatch at entry, e.g. by hiding or disabling annual-only promo codes when a monthly plan is selected, or by prompting a plan switch at the moment such a code is entered.
findings.location: Billing, promo code - second message block (plan mismatch)
